column4: Show each persona only its menus and screens
column6:
As a Business Administrator, I need BIBS to follow the identified user journeys, shown in a walkthrough, so that every persona works through screens that match the way BDOI works.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BR-002 (p.13); BR-181 (p.23); BR-182 (p.23); p.4 benefit 4a
* FRS: FRS BRD-00 Core Replacement v1.1 (BIBS_FRS_BRD-00_Core_Replacement_v1.1.docx), section 4.1 Navigation and persona menus, FR-CR-001 Show each persona only its menus and screens
* Persona: Every user
* Function: The sidebar lists the modules of BIBS. Each screen names the permission that opens it; a user sees only the screens that the permissions of his roles allow, in seven groups in a fixed order.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Roles and their permissions are changed only through an approved User Access request (BRD-11). (Configurable)
* (R2) A screen without a permission of the user is never shown, even if the user knows its address. (Fixed)
* Check: Screen without permission. Message: "You do not have access to this screen. Contact your administrator if you need it."

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the user is signed in, when BIBS reads the permissions of the user's roles, then a Cashiering user sees Operations and Finance > Cashiering and no Client & Policy screen.
* (AC2) Given the user is signed in, when BIBS reads the permissions of the user's roles, then a user with two roles sees the screens of both roles.
* (AC3) Given the user is signed in, when BIBS reads the permissions of the user's roles, then opening a screen by URL without its permission shows the no-access message.

*Out of scope / notes*
* No open clarification on this FR.

*Links*
* FRS section 4.1 Navigation and persona menus (BIBS_FRS_BRD-00_Core_Replacement_v1.1.docx)
* Screens: Sidebar menu (groups Home, Client & Policy, Operations, Finance, Claims & Insurance, Reports, Setup & Administration)
* Walkthrough step J1.1 (UAM requestor, approver, implementer): FRS BRD-11 walkthrough WT-A (A.1-A.8)
* Test cases: No test plan of its own (umbrella FRS); covered by the cases of the function test plans: TC-NB-011.1 to 011.3, 064.1 to 064.3, 010.1 to 010.3, 122.1 to 122.3 (19 cases)

column4: Notify users of status changes, approvals and pending work
column6:
As a Marketing AO, I need automated notifications, approvals and feedback tracking, so that approvals and feedback do not wait on e-mail.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: p.5 envisioned 5a; BR-083 (p.17); BR-111 (p.19); BR-206 (p.25)
* FRS: FRS BRD-00 Core Replacement v1.1 (BIBS_FRS_BRD-00_Core_Replacement_v1.1.docx), section 4.3 Notifications and workflow communication, FR-CR-020 Notify users of status changes, approvals and pending work
* Persona: System; every user
* Function: Workflow steps, approvals, returns, SLA breaches and job failures create in-system notifications for the users or roles concerned; selected events are also e-mailed (for example remittance schedules and confirmations, BR-083).

*Business rules*
* (R1) Notification events per module are those of the function FRS; the per-role catalogue is part of deliverable 15. (Configurable)
* (R2) Outbound documents that leave BDOI are password protected (FR-CR-071). (Fixed)

Product Maintenance adds no screen and no sign-in rule of its own (CLR-PM-23).

*Business rules*
* (R1) Log-in, lock-out and session rules follow the session policy of BRD-11 (FR-UA-001, 002; BRNB.040 of BRD-1). (Configurable)
* (R2) Directory sign-in follows BRD-11 - single sign-on through EIAM on Microsoft Entra ID with OpenID Connect or SAML 2.0, switched on by configuration (FR-UA-003); the lock-out after three attempts applies to local sign-in (CLR-PM-23). (Configurable)
* Check: User ID or password wrong. Message: "Invalid user name or password"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the user has an active BIBS account with at least one Product Maintenance role, when the user signs in on the Login screen (Sign in with the BDO identity provider, or user ID and password in local sign-in), then a user with valid credentials and a Product Maintenance role logs in and sees the Product Maintenance menu section.
* (AC2) Given the user has an active BIBS account with at least one Product Maintenance role, when the user signs in on the Login screen (Sign in with the BDO identity provider, or user ID and password in local sign-in), then a user with wrong credentials is refused and no session is created.
* (AC3) Given the user has an active BIBS account with at least one Product Maintenance role, when the user signs in on the Login screen (Sign in with the BDO identity provider, or user ID and password in local sign-in), then the account locks after three failed attempts (LOGIN_MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS).

column4: Maintain the product hierarchy
column6:
As an MBS user, I want a standard, reusable product structure (line, subline, type, subtype, coverage and peril), so that products are consistent and scalable across packaged and non-packaged products.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: PMADD01 (p.4)
* FRS: FRS BRD-03 Product Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-03_Product_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.2 Product structure and master data, FR-PM-010 Maintain the product hierarchy
* Persona: MBS (maintain), Business Administrator (authorise)
* Function: BIBS holds one product hierarchy for all packages. Level 1 is the product line (LOB, for example Motor, Fire). Level 2 is the cover type, with an optional subtype under it (depth at most 2). Level 3 is the product (risk code). Level 4 is the coverage / peril of the line, used in each package version.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Hierarchy levels: line > cover type > subtype (optional) > product; coverages / perils per line. (Fixed)
* (R2) A packaged product needs a cover type. (Fixed)
* (R3) Risk codes follow the pattern of their line (for example ^MTR\d(2)$) when the line has one. (Configurable)
* (R4) Coverage kinds: Section, Coverage, Peril, Extension. (Configurable)
* (R5) Every hierarchy record is maker-checker. (Fixed)
* Check: Packaged product without cover type. Message: "A package needs its cover type (PMADD01)"
* Check: Risk code does not match the line pattern. Message: "Risk code <code> does not follow the naming convention of <line>"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the user has PRODUCT_MAINTAIN and a packaged product without a cover type, when MBS creates or edits a line, cover type or subtype, coverage or product, then it cannot be saved.
* (AC2) Given the user has PRODUCT_MAINTAIN and a risk code that does not follow its line's pattern, when MBS creates or edits a line, cover type or subtype, coverage or product, then it is refused with PRODUCT_CODE_PATTERN.
* (AC3) Given the user has PRODUCT_MAINTAIN and a new coverage, when MBS creates or edits a line, cover type or subtype, coverage or product, then it is usable in package versions only after another user authorises it.

*Out of scope / notes*
* CLR-PM-01 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Risk-code naming per line (BRPM.003, PMADD01; FR-PM-010). Proposed: Each product line can carry a risk-code pattern. BIBS refuses a new risk code that does not follow the pattern of its line. Until BDOI states the conventions, no pattern is set and every well-formed code is accepted. Decision requested: State the naming convention of each line (PQ02, PM-Q49).
* CLR-PM-15 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Bulk upload of product masters (FR-PM-010, 014). Proposed: No bulk upload screen in Product Maintenance. The go-live load runs through the data migration (objects R01, R03-R05, R07); later changes are made on the screens under maker-checker. Decision requested: Confirm that no bulk upload of product masters is needed after go-live (PM-Q36).

column4: Maintain insurer-specific package terms
column6:

* Persona: MBS (on a draft version); TSU (through negotiated terms)
* Function: Each package version lists its insurers with role (Lead, Participant or Panel), share (co-insurance), rate and minimum premium. For each insurer and coverage, the version holds whether the coverage is included, the limit, sub-limit, deductible (amount, percent or wording) and the clauses that apply.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Insurer roles: Lead, Participant, Panel. (Fixed)
* (R2) When shares are used, they total 100%. (Fixed)
* (R3) Every insurer has a term for every included coverage before submission. (Fixed)
* (R4) Clauses come from the authorised clause library. (Fixed)
* (R5) A new-business transaction with an insurer outside a package's panel is refused. (Fixed)

* Check: Insurer lacks a term for an included coverage. Message: "Insurer <code> has no terms for coverage <coverage>"

* Persona: Marketing AO; TSU Officer
* Function: The requester enters the request type and scope, the client (client-specific packages) or programme name, the product line, cover type or existing package, the reason, the requested terms (sections, coverages with limits and deductibles, requested rate and dates) and the target insurers, and attaches documents.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Request numbers are PKR-<yyyy>-<n>. (Configurable)
* (R2) A NEW request names the cover type; other types name the existing package. (Fixed)
* (R3) A client-specific request names the client; a generic programme does not need one (PQ14). (Fixed)
* (R4) NEW and AMEND requests always negotiate; RETIRE never; UPDATE, RENEW and REACTIVATE choose on the form. (Fixed)
* (R5) Before submission, a request other than RETIRE has requested terms, a package end date and, when negotiated, at least one target insurer. (Fixed)
* (R6) The type of a saved request cannot change. (Fixed)

* Check: Line not selected. Message: "Select the product line"
* Check: Reason not selected. Message: "Select the reason"
* Check: NEW request without cover type. Message: "Select the cover type"
* Check: Other type without package. Message: "Select the package product of the <type> request"
* Check: Client-specific without client. Message: "Select the client of the client-specific package (PQ14)"
* Check: End date not after start date. Message: "The package end date must be after its start date"
* Check: Negative rate or amount. Message: "Rates and amounts cannot be negative"
* Check: Missing items on submit. Message: "Complete the request: <items>"

column4: Approve a package request (Marketing)
column6:

*Background*

* Persona: Marketing TL, TH or UH
* Function: A Marketing approver reviews the submitted request and approves it, which sends it to the TSU TL, or returns it to the requester with a reason. The BRD allows the TL, TH or UH to approve; BIBS accepts any one of them (PQ08).

*Business rules*
* (R1) The approver is never the maker or submitter of the request. (Fixed)
* (R2) One approval by TL, TH or UH is enough (a chain by segment or amount waits for PQ08). (Configurable)
* (R3) SLA 24 hours (default). (Configurable)

* Check: Return without reason. Message: "Select a reason for '<action>'"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the request is in FOR_MKT_APPROVAL and the user has PKG_REQUEST_APPROVE and is not the maker or submitter, when the approver opens the request from the For Approval tab, then the requester cannot approve their own request.

* (AC3) Given the request is in FOR_MKT_APPROVAL and the user has PKG_REQUEST_APPROVE and is not the maker or submitter and a returned request, when the approver opens the request from the For Approval tab, then it is back in DRAFT with the reason visible on the request.

column4: Prepare, approve and send the quotation slip
column6:
As a TSU Officer, I need to prepare the quotation slip from the request and send it to the insurers after its approval, so that every insurer receives the agreed terms and the communication is kept.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRPM.012 (p.22)
* FRS: FRS BRD-03 Product Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-03_Product_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.4 Negotiation and comparative tables, FR-PM-030 Prepare, approve and send the quotation slip
* Persona: TSU Officer (prepare); TSU TL or co-officer (approve)
* Function: The QS of each round is generated from the request, so the Marketing details flow into it; TSU edits the insurers and notes of the round. The preparer submits the QS, which gets a number PQS-yyyy-n and a reply due date. A TL or co-officer approves it, and BIBS then sends one protected e-mail per insurer and opens a pending response for each.

*Business rules*
* (R1) QS numbers are PQS-<yyyy>-<n>. (Configurable)
* (R2) Reply due date = send date + 5 days (default). (Configurable)
* (R3) The QS is approved by someone other than its preparer. (Fixed)
* (R4) One protected e-mail per insurer; the password is sent separately. (Fixed)
* (R5) Slips lock at the ManCom sign-off. (Fixed)
* Check: No insurer selected. Message: "Select at least one insurer for the quotation slip"
* Check: Approver is the preparer. Message: "The quotation slip is approved by a TL or a co-officer"
* Check: Edit after sign-off. Message: "The slips are locked since the ManCom sign-off"
* Check: Round already sent. Message: "Round <n> is already sent"
* Check: Resend of a closed round. Message: "Only the slip of an open, sent round can be resent"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the request is in NEGOTIATION; a round is open, when the TSU Officer opens the round and selects the insurers, then the preparer cannot approve their own QS.
* (AC2) Given the request is in NEGOTIATION; a round is open and an approved QS, when the TSU Officer opens the round and selects the insurers, then it is e-mailed to each insurer of the round as a protected PDF, and the E-mails tab lists each send.
* (AC3) Given the request is in NEGOTIATION; a round is open, when the TSU Officer opens the round and selects the insurers, then the officer can view the sent history and resend to one insurer.

column4: Record insurer responses and outcomes
column6:
As a TSU Officer, I need to key in each insurer's terms and feedback and edit them later, so that the responses are reviewed and approved before they go to Marketing.

*Background*

* Function: TSU keys in each insurer's reply per round, with the outcome, the offered rate and minimum premium, the terms per coverage (included, limit, deductible, clauses), conditions and warranties, validity and remarks, and attaches the insurer's reply. * (R3) Every change to a response is kept in its history. (Fixed)

* Check: Negative rate or premium. Message: "Rates and amounts cannot be negative"

* (AC1) Given the QS of the round has been sent to the insurer, when the officer opens the insurer's response in the round, then TSU records "Approved with changes" with a rate and changed deductibles for one insurer and "Declined" for another.
* (AC2) Given the QS of the round has been sent to the insurer and a counter-proposal without a rate, when the officer opens the insurer's response in the round, then it is refused.

column4: Run further negotiation rounds
column6:
As a TSU Officer, I need to negotiate terms, rates and conditions with insurers and record the outcome, so that a package is not finalised before the negotiation is complete and documented.

*Background*

* Persona: TSU Officer / TL
* Function: When terms need another round, TSU clicks Revise Quotation Slip. BIBS closes the sent round and opens round n+1, by default with the insurers that did not decline, and the new QS goes through the same approval and sending (FR-PM-030). All rounds and their responses stay on the request.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Round n+1 proposes the insurers of round n that did not decline. (Fixed)
* (R2) There is no maximum number of rounds until BDOI states one (PQ05). (Configurable)
* (R3) Not-proceeded reasons: declined by the insurers, terms not accepted, client withdrew, business decision, others. (Configurable)
* Check: Revise before the current QS is sent. Message: "Send the slip of round <n> first"
* Check: Not proceeded without reason. Message: "Select a reason for '<action>'"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the request is in NEGOTIATION and the latest round has been sent and a request negotiated in two rounds, when the officer clicks Revise Quotation Slip and states what changes in this round, then it shows both rounds, their QS numbers and the responses of each.
* (AC2) Given the request is in NEGOTIATION and the latest round has been sent, when the officer clicks Revise Quotation Slip and states what changes in this round, then Round 2 opens by default without the insurers that declined in round 1.
* (AC3) Given the request is in NEGOTIATION and the latest round has been sent and a request closed as not proceeded, when the officer clicks Revise Quotation Slip and states what changes in this round, then it shows the reason and cannot be reopened.

column4: Compile one comparative master per package request
column6:
As a TSU Officer, I need all insurers' feedback compiled automatically into one comparative table per package, so that the terms can be compared, exported and shared by authorised users.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRPM.014 (p.24-25); BRPM.013 (p.23)
* FRS: FRS BRD-03 Product Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-03_Product_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.4 Negotiation and comparative tables, FR-PM-034 Compile one comparative master per package request
* Persona: System; TSU
* Function: BIBS compiles all insurer responses of the latest round into one comparative table per request, showing outcome, rate, minimum premium, coverages, deductibles, conditions, validity and remarks per insurer. A new master supersedes the previous one, so there is only one current master; earlier masters stay as superseded outputs. Each output is stored as a PDF and XLSX attachment with its hash. Marketing sees it read-only.

*Business rules*
* (R1) One current MASTER per request. (Fixed)
* (R2) An output is rendered from the values stored at generation, so a file downloaded later shows the same content. (Fixed)
* (R3) Marketing has view-only access to comparative tables. (Fixed)
* Check: Compile before the quotation slip of the round is sent. Message: "Send the quotation slip of round <n> first"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the quotation slip of the latest round has been sent and a request with three responses, when BIBS compiles the master at Terms Final, or TSU clicks Compile Master during negotiation, then it has one current master listing the three insurers with their terms.
* (AC2) Given the quotation slip of the latest round has been sent, when BIBS compiles the master at Terms Final, or TSU clicks Compile Master during negotiation, then after a second compilation the first master is marked superseded and is still downloadable.
* (AC3) Given the quotation slip of the latest round has been sent, when BIBS compiles the master at Terms Final, or TSU clicks Compile Master during negotiation, then a Marketing user can open the master but has no Compile or Generate buttons.

column4: Validate and release a package version
column6:
As the TSU Head or Business Administrator, I want an explicit validation checkpoint after set-up, so that an incorrect configuration does not reach New Business.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: PMADD06 (p.5); BRPM.015 (p.25-26)
* FRS: FRS BRD-03 Product Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-03_Product_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.5 Sign-off, set-up and release, FR-PM-043 Validate and release a package version
* Persona: TSU Head or Business Administrator (PRODUCT_VALIDATE)
* Function: A package version is not ready until it is validated. MBS submits the draft; BIBS checks completeness. The validator, who is neither the maker nor the submitter, confirms the checklist, reviews a test premium computed on a sample item, and releases the version or returns it with a reason.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Checklist: hierarchy complete (cover type and basic coverage); every panel insurer has terms for each included coverage; rates and minimum premiums match the signed-off terms; dates and package term are correct; test premium reviewed (final list PQ09). (Configurable)
* (R2) The validator is never the maker or submitter of the version. (Fixed)
* (R3) The effective date is today or later and after the latest released version. (Fixed)
* (R4) Only RELEASED versions are sold. (Fixed)
* (R5) SLA 24 hours (default). (Configurable)
* Check: Hierarchy incomplete. Message: "A package needs its cover type (PMADD01)"
* Check: Insurer terms missing. Message: "Insurer <code> has no terms for coverage <coverage>"
* Check: No rate. Message: "Enter the package rate or a rate for every insurer"
* Check: No effective date. Message: "Enter the effective date"
* Check: Validator is maker or submitter. Message: "A package version is validated by someone other than its maker and submitter"
* Check: Checklist not complete. Message: "Validate and Release stays disabled until every item is ticked"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the version is FOR_VALIDATION, when the validator opens the version from the Validation Queue, then the MBS user who set up the version cannot validate it.
* (AC2) Given the version is FOR_VALIDATION and a released version, when the validator opens the version from the Validation Queue, then it is used by new quotations from its effective date; before release it is not.
* (AC3) Given the version is FOR_VALIDATION and a returned version, when the validator opens the version from the Validation Queue, then it is editable again and the request is back with MBS.

column4: Draft and send package advisories

* Function: On release BIBS drafts the advisory automatically, a new package advisory for a new or reactivated package, a renewal advisory for a renewal, a package update advisory otherwise, and a retirement advisory for a retired package. The user checks the recipients, subject and text and sends it. Sending is blocked until the supporting documents are on the request. Recipients receive an in-app notification, and e-mail addresses given on the advisory receive the protected advisory PDF.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Required documents: signed package slip (PKG_SLIP_SIGNED) and ManCom sign-off (MANCOM_SIGNOFF); for a retirement only the ManCom sign-off. (Fixed)
* (R2) Recipient groups: Marketing, TSU, MBS, Processing, Operations; default Marketing, TSU, MBS, Operations. (Configurable)
* (R3) Group to users: Marketing = quotation users, TSU = PKG_NEGOTIATE, MBS = PRODUCT_MAINTAIN, Processing = account processing, Operations = OPS_VIEW (PQ12). (Fixed)

column4: Keep package terms as versions
column6:
As a Marketing AO, I need new business priced automatically on the latest approved rate scheme, so that an outdated rate cannot be selected.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRPM.007 (p.17-18)
* FRS: FRS BRD-03 Product Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-03_Product_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.6 Versions and rate schemes, FR-PM-050 Keep package terms as versions
* Persona: MBS; System
* Function: The commercial terms of a package (rate scheme, coverages, insurers, insurer terms, dates) are held in numbered versions with an effective date. A package is never edited in place. MBS creates a new draft version, which is validated and released while the current version keeps selling. The Versions tab shows the timeline and compares two versions.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Version states: Draft, For validation, Released, Superseded, Expired (section 5.3). (Fixed)
* (R2) One released version is in force per product; the previous one ends the day before the next takes effect. (Fixed)

* (R2) Reminders at 30 and 7 days (default). (Configurable)

column4: Log in with a persona profile from a BDO-issued device
column6:
As a Requestor, I need to access the application using any BDO-issued device (Log in as a Requestor), so that only authorised staff on BDO devices reach BIBS and an unattended session is closed safely.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRD 1.001.1 (p.8); BRD 1.001.1.1 (p.8); BRD 2.001.1 (p.8); BRD 2.001.1.1 (p.8); BRD 3.001.1 (p.9); BRD 3.001.1.1 (p.9); BRD 4.001.1 (p.9); BRD 4.001.1.1 (p.9); UAM-NFR-18 (p.14); UAM-NFR-19 (p.14)
* FRS: FRS BRD-11 User Access Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-11_User_Access_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.1 Sign-in, session and password, FR-UA-001 Log in with a persona profile from a BDO-issued device
* Persona: Requestor, Approver, Business Administrator, System Administrator
* Function: Users sign in to BIBS in a browser with their user ID and password. BIBS checks the credentials and the account status, counts failed attempts and locks the account after LOGIN_MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS failed attempts (3, for every BIBS user). Every successful and failed attempt is written to the audit trail. The menu shows only the screens of the user's roles.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Lock-out after LOGIN_MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS consecutive failures (3); applies to all users (CQ23 answered by this BRD). (Configurable)
* (R2) A user may hold several roles; the menu is the union of their screens (NFR 1.c-d). (Fixed)
* Check: User ID or password wrong. Message: "Invalid user name or password"
* Check: Account locked (the same message as a wrong password; the lock shows to the System Administrator on Users). Message: "Invalid user name or password"
* Check: Account deactivated (the same message as a wrong password; the status shows to the System Administrator on Users). Message: "Invalid user name or password"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the user has an enabled BIBS account with at least one role, when the user opens BIBS from a BDO-issued device and enters the user ID and password, then a user with the Requestor profile logs in and sees the User Access screens of the Requestor only.
* (AC2) Given the user has an enabled BIBS account with at least one role, when the user opens BIBS from a BDO-issued device and enters the user ID and password, then the third wrong password locks the account; the fourth attempt, with the correct password, is refused with the same message as a wrong password ("Invalid user name or password"), and Users shows the account as locked to the System Administrator.
* (AC3) Given the user has an enabled BIBS account with at least one role, when the user opens BIBS from a BDO-issued device and enters the user ID and password, then a deactivated user is refused with the same message as a wrong password ("Invalid user name or password") and the count of failed attempts does not change.
* (AC4) Given the user has an enabled BIBS account with at least one role, when the user opens BIBS from a BDO-issued device and enters the user ID and password, then the audit trail lists the failed and successful attempts.

*Out of scope / notes*
* CLR-UA-17 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Access from BDO-issued devices only (1.001.1; FR-UA-001). Proposed: Access only from BDO-issued devices is enforced by the BDO network and device policy, not by BIBS. Decision requested: BDOI IT to confirm the network and device policy that enforces it (UA-Q10).
* CLR-UA-25 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Lock-out, second factor and BDO devices with EIAM (BRD 1.001.1, UAM-NFR-19; FR-UA-001, 003). Proposed: For users who sign in through EIAM, Entra ID enforces the password, the lock-out, the second factor and the BDO-device rule (conditional access); BIBS does not ask a second code after the single sign-on. The BIBS lock-out after 3 attempts and the BIBS second factor stay for local accounts. Decision requested: BDOI IT and Information Security to confirm that the Entra ID policies meet the BRD rules (UA-Q10, UA-Q15).

column4: Warn before the inactivity and system log-out
column6:
As a Requestor, I need to receive the inactivity warning (15 minutes) (Log in as a Requestor), so that only authorised staff on BDO devices reach BIBS and an unattended session is closed safely.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRD 1.001.1.2 (p.8); BRD 1.001.1.3 (p.8); BRD 2.001.1.2 (p.8); BRD 2.001.1.3 (p.8); BRD 3.001.1.2 (p.9); BRD 3.001.1.3 (p.9); BRD 4.001.1.2 (p.9); BRD 4.001.1.3 (p.9); UAM-NFR-34 (p.17)

* Persona: All users
* Function: After 15 minutes without activity BIBS shows a warning; after 30 minutes without activity it signs the user out. Activity in any browser tab keeps all tabs signed in. *Business rules*
* (R1) Inactivity warning after SESSION_IDLE_WARNING_MINUTES (15). (Configurable)
* (R2) Inactivity sign-out after SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES (30). (Configurable)
* (R3) Warning SESSION_EXPIRY_WARNING_MINUTES (30) before the fixed session expiry. (Configurable)

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the user is signed in, when the user stops working for 15 minutes; BIBS shows the inactivity warning, then after 15 minutes without activity the warning appears.
* (AC2) Given the user is signed in, when the user stops working for 15 minutes; BIBS shows the inactivity warning, then after 30 minutes without activity the user is signed out.

column4: Sign in with the BDO account (single sign-on through EIAM)
column6:
As a BIBS user, I need to sign in with my BDO directory account (EIAM, Microsoft Entra ID), so that I use one BDO identity and BIBS keeps no password for me.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: UAM-NFR-11 (p.13); UAM-NFR-17 (p.14); UAM-NFR-33 (p.17)
* FRS: FRS BRD-11 User Access Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-11_User_Access_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.1 Sign-in, session and password, FR-UA-003 Sign in with the BDO account (single sign-on through EIAM)
* Persona: All users; System
* Function: The BRD asks for sign-in with the Windows ID checked by BDO EUA (p.14), for LDAP or Active Directory authentication (p.13) and for integration with single sign-on (SSO) or LDAP (p.17). BDOI named EIAM, BDO's Enterprise Identity Access Management on Microsoft Entra ID, as the sign-in of BDO users for Drop 0 (decisions of 26 September 2026).

*Business rules*
* (R1) Sign-in mode LOCAL, DIRECTORY, OIDC or SAML; the identity provider, its registration and the claim that identifies the user are set per environment. (Configurable)
* (R2) Authorisation (roles and permissions) stays in BIBS in every mode; no group of the identity provider is mapped to a BIBS role, and an external ACL is on hold (UQ14, CLR-UA-26). (Fixed)
* (R3) In OIDC or SAML mode only the named break-glass System Administrators sign in with a local password, always with the second factor; every such sign-in is alerted to Information Security (CLR-UA-24). (Configurable)
* (R4) The returned identity is matched to the Windows ID held on the user, or to the user principal name where the Windows ID is not released (proposed, CLR-UA-22). (Configurable)
* Check: The identity is not linked to an active user. Message: "Your sign-in was accepted by your organisation, but it is not linked to an active user of this system. Contact your administrator."
* Check: The identity provider could not complete the sign-in. Message: "Your organisation’s sign-in service could not complete the sign-in. Try again in a moment."
* Check: Single sign-on not set up in the environment. Message: "Single sign-on is not available. Contact your administrator."
* Check: DIRECTORY mode - the directory refuses the log-on. Message: "The message returned by the directory"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given AUTH_MODE = OIDC or SAML, with BIBS registered in EIAM; the user exists in BIBS, is active and carries the Windows ID or UPN that EIAM returns (FR-UA-052), when the user opens BIBS and clicks Sign in with the BDO identity provider on the Login page, then in OIDC mode a user signs in with the BDO account at EIAM and BIBS opens the session with the user's BIBS roles; BIBS stores no password for the user.
* (AC2) Given AUTH_MODE = OIDC or SAML, with BIBS registered in EIAM; the user exists in BIBS, is active and carries the Windows ID or UPN that EIAM returns (FR-UA-052), when the user opens BIBS and clicks Sign in with the BDO identity provider on the Login page, then an identity that is not linked to an active BIBS user is refused with the message SSO_NOT_LINKED and the attempt is audited.
* (AC3) Given AUTH_MODE = OIDC or SAML, with BIBS registered in EIAM; the user exists in BIBS, is active and carries the Windows ID or UPN that EIAM returns (FR-UA-052), when the user opens BIBS and clicks Sign in with the BDO identity provider on the Login page, then in OIDC mode a break-glass System Administrator signs in with the local password and the second factor; another user cannot sign in with a local password.
* (AC4) Given AUTH_MODE = OIDC or SAML, with BIBS registered in EIAM; the user exists in BIBS, is active and carries the Windows ID or UPN that EIAM returns (FR-UA-052), when the user opens BIBS and clicks Sign in with the BDO identity provider on the Login page, then the menu after a single sign-on is that of the user's BIBS roles, whatever groups the identity provider holds.

*Out of scope / notes*
* CLR-UA-01 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Single sign-on through EIAM (UAM-NFR-11, 17, 33; FR-UA-003). Proposed: Single sign-on with OpenID Connect against the BDO Entra ID tenant (EIAM), SAML 2.0 kept as the fall-back if the BDOI IT standards require it. It is part of BIBS and switched on by configuration (sign-in mode OIDC or SAML) once BDOI IT registers BIBS for each environment; SIT uses local sign-in until then. Not a change request. Decision requested: BDOI IT to choose the protocol and to register BIBS in EIAM for each environment, with test accounts for SIT and UAT (UA-Q06, UA-Q07, IQ04).
* CLR-UA-02 - open, for BDOI confirmation: External access-control list (UAM-NFR-12; FR-UA-003). Proposed: Roles and permissions are kept in BIBS; there is no authorisation through an external access-control list. Decision requested: Confirm that authorisation stays in BIBS, or specify the external ACL (UQ14, UA-Q23).
* CLR-UA-21 - open, for BDOI confirmation: EIAM replaces the EUA and LDAP sign-in (UAM-NFR-11, 17; FR-UA-003). Proposed: EIAM on Microsoft Entra ID is the only directory sign-in of BDO users; the EUA password check and the LDAP / Active Directory sign-in are closed as replaced by EIAM, and the sign-in mode DIRECTORY is not used. Local sign-in is kept only for the break-glass administrators (CLR-UA-24). Decision requested: Confirm that EIAM replaces EUA and LDAP / AD for every BDO user (UA-Q05).
* CLR-UA-22 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Matching the EIAM account to the BIBS user (UAM-NFR-15, 17; FR-UA-003, 052). Proposed: EIAM returns the Windows ID in a dedicated claim (or the user principal name where the Windows ID is not released); BIBS matches it to the Windows ID held on each user. The BIBS user ID stays the employee-number format (a999999999). An account with no matching active user is refused with the message SSO_NOT_LINKED. Decision requested: BDOI IT to confirm the claim that identifies the user and the relation of the Windows ID to the user ID (UA-Q08, UA-Q25).
* CLR-UA-24 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Break-glass administrators (FR-UA-003, 006). Proposed: Two named System Administrator accounts keep a local password and the BIBS second factor; their credentials are sealed by Information Security, every sign-in is alerted to Information Security and reviewed monthly; single sign-on is switched on only once these accounts exist. Decision requested: Information Security to confirm the number, the holders and the review (UA-Q13).
* CLR-UA-25 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Lock-out, second factor and BDO devices with EIAM (BRD 1.001.1, UAM-NFR-19; FR-UA-001, 003). Proposed: For users who sign in through EIAM, Entra ID enforces the password, the lock-out, the second factor and the BDO-device rule (conditional access); BIBS does not ask a second code after the single sign-on. The BIBS lock-out after 3 attempts and the BIBS second factor stay for local accounts. Decision requested: BDOI IT and Information Security to confirm that the Entra ID policies meet the BRD rules (UA-Q10, UA-Q15).
* CLR-UA-26 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Roles stay in BIBS with single sign-on (FR-UA-003). Proposed: Group profiles and permissions stay in BIBS and change only by BIBS requests; no Entra ID group is mapped to a BIBS role. EIAM may restrict who reaches BIBS through an assignment to a 'BIBS users' group kept by BDOI IT. Decision requested: Confirm that roles are not taken from Entra ID groups (UA-Q09).

column4: Log out and keep a session log
column6:
As the System Administrator, I need the Windows ID, user name, status, business unit group and user level on every user, so that each user is identified and classified.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: UAM-NFR-35 (p.17); UAM-NFR-15 (p.14)
* FRS: FRS BRD-11 User Access Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-11_User_Access_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.1 Sign-in, session and password, FR-UA-004 Log out and keep a session log
* Persona: All users; System Administrator
* Function: Log-in and failed log-in are audited. Log Out ends the session in BIBS and records LOGOUT in the audit trail. Every session is kept in a session log - user, start, last activity, end and end reason (log-out, inactivity, session expiry, ended by an administrator, account locked). The user list shows a user as Online while a session is open (UQ13).

*Business rules*
* (R1) Last activity is updated at most every 5 minutes. (Fixed)
* (R2) Single session per device is not enforced; the session log prepares it (UQ09). (Fixed)
* (R3) In single sign-on, Log Out also ends the user's EIAM session (proposed rule, CLR-UA-23; BDOI IT confirms that this is acceptable to the other BDO applications that share the session). (Configurable)

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the user is signed in, when the user clicks Log Out, then after Log Out, the audit log report shows the log-out with user and time.
* (AC2) Given the user is signed in, when the user clicks Log Out, then the Users screen shows a signed-in user as Online.
* (AC3) Given the user is signed in, when the user clicks Log Out, then in single sign-on, after Log Out the user is at the EIAM sign-out page, and opening BIBS again asks for the BDO sign-in.

*Out of scope / notes*
* CLR-UA-09 - open, for BDOI confirmation: One session per device (UAM-NFR-35; FR-UA-004). Proposed: The session log records every session; one session per device is not enforced. Decision requested: Decide whether one session per device must be enforced (UQ09, UA-Q44).
* CLR-UA-23 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Log Out ends the EIAM session (UAM-NFR-35; FR-UA-004). Proposed: Log Out ends the BIBS session, records it in the session log and sends the user to the EIAM sign-out page, so the BDO session ends too; after an inactivity sign-out the next sign-in goes through EIAM again. Decision requested: BDOI IT to confirm that single sign-out is acceptable, and the re-authentication after an inactivity sign-out (UA-Q11, UA-Q12).

column4: Enforce the password policy and self-service reset
column6:
As a BIBS user with a local account, I need to change my password and have it reset by the administrator, so that I keep access securely.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: UAM-NFR-31 (p.17); UAM-NFR-36 (p.17); UAM-NFR-37 (p.17)
* FRS: FRS BRD-11 User Access Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-11_User_Access_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.1 Sign-in, session and password, FR-UA-005 Enforce the password policy and self-service reset
* Persona: All users (local accounts); System Administrator
* Function: Users change their own password on My Profile; the password has at least 10 characters with upper and lower case letters, a digit and a symbol. The System Administrator resets a password and BIBS shows a temporary password once.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Length and complexity - at least 10 characters, upper and lower case, digit, symbol. (Fixed)
* (R2) History 8, maximum age 90 days, minimum age 1 day (values of the Collections NFR, to confirm, UQ08). (Configurable)
* (R3) Reset links are single-use and expire after 30 minutes. (Fixed)
* Check: Current password wrong. Message: "Current password is incorrect"
* Check: New password too weak. Message: "Still needed: At least 10 characters; An upper-case letter; A lower-case letter; A digit; A symbol (on the screen, as the user types)"
* Check: Password used before. Message: "You used this password recently. Choose another one"
* Check: Changed too soon. Message: "You changed your password less than a day ago"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given AUTH_MODE = LOCAL and a new password equal to one of the last 8, when the user opens My Profile and enters the current and the new password twice, then it is refused.
* (AC2) Given AUTH_MODE = LOCAL, when the user opens My Profile and enters the current and the new password twice, then after an administrator reset, the user must change the password at the next log-in.
* (AC3) Given AUTH_MODE = LOCAL, when the user opens My Profile and enters the current and the new password twice, then the reset link works once and not after 30 minutes.

column4: Deactivate dormant users
column6:
As the Information Security Officer, I need four eyes on every access change, least privilege, separation-of-duties rules and the deactivation of dormant users, so that BIBS meets the BSP, AMLA and Data Privacy Act requirements.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: UAM-NFR-06 (p.12); UAM-NFR-09 (p.13)
* FRS: FRS BRD-11 User Access Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-11_User_Access_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.1 Sign-in, session and password, FR-UA-006 Deactivate dormant users
* Persona: System (daily job); Requestor (told of the result)
* Function: Every night BIBS deactivates the users who have not signed in for UAM_DORMANT_DAYS days (90), counted from the last sign-in, or from the creation or the last reactivation when later. UAM_DORMANT_NOTICE_DAYS days before (7) the user is told to sign in. Each deactivation is a Deactivate user request with the reason "No sign-in for the dormancy period", approved and applied by the system, so it has the request history, the change log and the notice to the user like any other request. The holders of the System Administrator profile are never deactivated this way.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Dormancy period 90 days; 0 switches the job off. (Configurable)
* (R2) Notice 7 days before; 0 sends no notice. (Configurable)
* (R3) The System Administrator profile is never deactivated by the job, so the administration stays reachable. (Fixed)

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given UAM_DORMANT_DAYS is more than 0, when the job finds the active users without a sign-in for the dormancy period, then a user without a sign-in for 91 days is deactivated by the job with a request whose reason is "No sign-in for the dormancy period".
* (AC2) Given UAM_DORMANT_DAYS is more than 0, when the job finds the active users without a sign-in for the dormancy period, then a user whose deactivation date is 7 days away receives the notice and stays active.

*Out of scope / notes*
* CLR-UA-08 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Dormant accounts (information security practice; FR-UA-006). Proposed: A daily deactivation of users with no sign-in for 90 days, with a notice 7 days before; the System Administrator profile is exempt. Decision requested: Information Security to confirm the dormancy period and the notice (template CI-05, UA-Q42).
* CLR-UA-24 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Break-glass administrators (FR-UA-003, 006). Proposed: Two named System Administrator accounts keep a local password and the BIBS second factor; their credentials are sealed by Information Security, every sign-in is alerted to Information Security and reviewed monthly; single sign-on is switched on only once these accounts exist. Decision requested: Information Security to confirm the number, the holders and the review (UA-Q13).

* (R3) Only one open request (DRAFT excluded) per user or per group profile. (Fixed)
* (R4) Remarks (justification) are mandatory on submission, up to 1000 characters. (Fixed)
* (R5) Requests are never deleted; a cancelled request stays visible with its reason. (Fixed)

column4: Approve a request and grant the access
column6:
As an Approver, I need to approve the request (Review and Approve Requests), so that every access change is decided by a second person with the reason recorded.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRD 2.002.5 (p.8); p.6 "System to grant the access"
* FRS: FRS BRD-11 User Access Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-11_User_Access_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.3 Review and approval (Approver), FR-UA-031 Approve a request and grant the access
* Persona: Approver; System
* Function: Approve and Apply records the decision and applies the change - creates the user, changes the user data or group profiles, disables or enables the user - and notifies the requester. For a new user BIBS shows a temporary password once; it is never stored in clear. Neither the requester nor the subject user can approve. After approval, a request with a risk flag goes to the second approver (FR-UA-034); a request with a future effective date becomes SCHEDULED (FR-UA-020); a group-profile request goes to the next approver or to the System Administrator (FR-UA-044, FR-UA-045). Every applied attribute is logged with from and to values (FR-UA-064), and the affected user is notified.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Four eyes - the requester and the subject user never decide. (Fixed)
* (R2) The temporary password of a new user is shown once to the approver (LOCAL mode). (Fixed)
* (R3) The applied change is checked again at approval (the user or role may have changed since submission). (Fixed)
* (R4) An enrolment is approved on its own, from its page: Approve Selected on Access Requests cannot select it and My Approvals refuses it, so its temporary password is always shown to the approver. (Fixed)
* Check: Approver is the requester. Message: "A request cannot be decided by the user who submitted it"
* Check: Approver is the subject user. Message: "You cannot decide a request about your own access"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the request is PENDING and assigned to the user (or UAM_ANY_APPROVER); the user has ACCESS_APPROVE and is neither the requester nor the subject user and an approved enrolment, when the approver reviews the request and enters an optional comment, then it creates the user and shows the temporary password once.
* (AC2) Given the request is PENDING and assigned to the user (or UAM_ANY_APPROVER); the user has ACCESS_APPROVE and is neither the requester nor the subject user, when the approver reviews the request and enters an optional comment, then the requester cannot approve his or her own request (ACCESS_FOUR_EYES).

column4: Escalate privileged and out-of-hours changes for a second approval
column6:

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: UAM-NFR-40 (p.17)
* FRS: FRS BRD-11 User Access Maintenance v2.1 (02_BIBS_FRS_BRD-11_User_Access_Maintenance_v2.1.docx), section 4.3 Review and approval (Approver), FR-UA-034 Escalate privileged and out-of-hours changes for a second approval
* Persona: System; Second approver (UAM_SECOND_APPROVE)
* Function: The BRD asks that changes to user privileges are monitored, evaluated and escalated for additional review, for example modifications outside working hours or from low to high privilege (p.17).

*Business rules*
* (R1) Privilege level per group profile; SYSADMIN is ADMIN; the high-privilege profiles are UQ07. (Configurable)
* (R2) Working hours 08:00-18:00 Monday to Friday (to confirm, UQ07). (Configurable)
* (R3) The second approver differs from the first approver, the requester and the subject user. (Fixed)
* Check: Second approver is the first approver. Message: "The second approval is given by another approver"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given a request has a risk flag and the first approver approved it, when BIBS sets the request to PENDING_SECOND and raises the alert, then a request that adds the System Administrator profile to a user needs a second approval.
* (AC2) Given a request has a risk flag and the first approver approved it and a request submitted at 21:00 on a weekday, when BIBS sets the request to PENDING_SECOND and raises the alert, then it is flagged OUTSIDE_HOURS.

* CLR-UA-14 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Out-of-hours flag on public holidays (NFR 11; FR-UA-034). * Persona: Business Administrator

The request has drafts and approvers in order, and after approval waits for the System Administrator (FR-UA-045), unless UAM_ROLE_APPLY_ON_APPROVAL is true (UQ03). *Business rules*

As a Business Administrator, I need to submit a User Access Group Profiles deactivation request (Submit a User Access Group Profile Request), so that group profiles are created and changed only under approval and implemented by the System Administrator.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRD 3.002.3 (p.9); BRD 3.002.3.1 (p.9); BRD 3.002.3.2 (p.9); BRD 3.002.3.4 (p.9); BRD 3.002.3.5 (p.9); BRD 3.002.3.6 (p.9); BRD 3.002.3.7 (p.9); BRD 3.002.3.8 (p.9)

* Persona: Business Administrator

* Persona: Business Administrator (maker); Information Security Officer (checker)
* Function: BIBS keeps the requester, the approver and the implementer of a request apart. The Business Administrator also records the pairs of group profiles that one user may not hold together, with the reason. Each new rule and each deactivation waits for the authorisation of Information Security (maker-checker). * (R1) The maker of a rule or of its deactivation never authorises it. (Fixed)
* (R2) One rule per pair of profiles; the order of the two profiles does not matter. (Fixed)
* (R3) The rules are checked on single requests, bulk lines and again at approval; existing users are not changed by a new rule and are found with the reports. (Fixed)
* Check: Same profile twice. Message: "Choose two different group profiles"
* Check: Rule exists. Message: "A rule for these two group profiles already exists"
* Check: Maker authorises. Message: "A record cannot be authorized by the user who maintained it"

* (AC2) Given the maker has UAM_SOD_MAINTAIN; the checker has UAM_SOD_AUTHORIZE, when the Business Administrator opens Separation of Duties, chooses New Rule, selects the two group profiles and enters the reason, then the Business Administrator who created the rule cannot authorise it.

* (R4) An object loads only after every object it depends on is accepted in the same environment (gate G6). (Fixed)

* Check: No rationale. Message: "Enter the rationale for the proposed class"

* Persona: Data owner, Data Steward, Data Migration Lead, reconciliation approver
* Function: Every object passes seven gates, each recorded with the role, user, decision, comment, time and evidence. The gates are G1 Decision, G2 Mapping, G3 Validation, G4 Load approval, G5 Reconciliation, G6 Object accepted and G7 Go-live.

column4: Receive a source extract with control totals
column6:
As the Data Migration Lead, I need to reconcile all migrated data per data object, so that every data object and item is reconcilable from source to target after the cut-over.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRID_MIG 1.2 (p.7)
* FRS: Data Migration Handbook BRD-13 Data Migration v2.1 (02_BIBS_Handbook_BRD-13_Data_Migration_v2.1.docx), section 20.2 Extract intake, code maps, validation and load, FR-DM-010 Receive a source extract with control totals
* Persona: Migration Operator
* Function: BDOI sends one file per layout and source system with a control file. Most objects have one layout; R04 (insurers and insurer branches R04B), P01 (headers and insurer shares P01S) and F01 (invoice headers, insurer shares F01S and components F01C) have sub-layouts sent as separate files with the same as-of date. BIBS checks each file before any row is staged, so that what BIBS loads is exactly what BDOI extracted.

*Business rules*
* (R1) File names are <LAYOUT>_<SOURCE>_<yyyyMMdd>_<nn>.csv or .xlsx, where LAYOUT is the layout code (for example F01C), not the object code; the control file adds .ctl.csv. (Fixed)
* (R5) A batch of an object takes one checked extract of each of its layouts with the same as-of date. (Fixed)
* (R2) CSV is UTF-8 with comma separator and one header row; dates are yyyy-MM-dd; amounts use a dot decimal and 2 decimals without thousands separator. (Fixed)
* (R3) Outside production, names, addresses, TIN, ID, account and phone numbers, e-mail addresses and birth dates are masked before staging; the same value is always masked the same way. (Configurable)
* (R4) Files are received through the console or the secure file drop and are never e-mailed. (Fixed)
* Check: Checksum differs. Message: "The file does not match the checksum in the control file"
* Check: Header differs from the layout. Message: "The file columns do not match layout version (n): missing (columns), extra (columns)"
* Check: Row count differs. Message: "The file has (n) rows; the control file says (m)"
* Check: Amount total differs. Message: "The total of (column) in (currency) is (x); the control file says (y)"
* Check: Hash total differs. Message: "The hash total of the key column does not match the control file"
* Check: Duplicate file. Message: "This file was already received as extract (no)"
* Check: As-of date out of order. Message: "The as-of date is earlier than the last extract of this object"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the object is Decided (Migrate or Carry-forward) and has an approved layout version and the user has the right "Data migration intake", when the operator opens Extracts, chooses the object, the layout and the source system and uploads the data file and the control file, then a file whose rows, amounts and hash total agree with its control file is staged and numbered.
* (AC2) Given the object is Decided (Migrate or Carry-forward) and has an approved layout version and the user has the right "Data migration intake" and a file with one row fewer than the control count, when the operator opens Extracts, chooses the object, the layout and the source system and uploads the data file and the control file, then it is rejected and nothing is staged.
* (AC3) Given the object is Decided (Migrate or Carry-forward) and has an approved layout version and the user has the right "Data migration intake", when the operator opens Extracts, chooses the object, the layout and the source system and uploads the data file and the control file, then in a non-production environment the staged client names and TINs are masked; in production they are not.

column4: Maintain and approve versioned code maps
column6:
As the Data Steward, I need governed mapping and migration of all identified reference data (lists of values, insurer, product, package and risk codes, MIS values, payees), so that transactions, disbursement and reporting use the correct codes and classifications.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRID_MIG 3.1 (p.9)
* FRS: Data Migration Handbook BRD-13 Data Migration v2.1 (02_BIBS_Handbook_BRD-13_Data_Migration_v2.1.docx), section 20.2 Extract intake, code maps, validation and load, FR-DM-011 Maintain and approve versioned code maps
* Persona: Data Steward (maker); data owner (approver)
* Function: A code map set exists per domain, for example each LOV type, insurers, insurer branches, products and risk codes, packages, lines, branches, sales units, account officers, each MIS field, GL accounts and the status lists of each object. An entry maps a legacy code of a source system to a BIBS code, or says Default, Reject or Create.

*Business rules*
* (R1) One approved version per set; a batch uses the approved version current at validation. (Fixed)
* (R2) The approver is never the user who submitted the version. (Fixed)
* (R3) An entry action is Map (to a target code), Default (to the set default), Reject (the row fails) or Create (a new BIBS value). (Fixed)
* (R4) The target code of a MAP entry must exist and be active in BIBS when the version is approved. (Fixed)
* Check: Target code does not exist. Message: "Target code (code) does not exist in (domain)"
* Check: Same legacy code twice. Message: "Legacy code (code) of (source) is mapped twice"
* Check: Approver is the submitter. Message: "A record cannot be authorized by the user who maintained it"

column4: Validate staged data against data-quality rules
column6:
As a Marketing User, I need the client master available in BIBS, so that I can service clients, renew policies and create new transactions without re-encoding identities.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRID_MIG 1.2 (p.7); BRID_MIG 2.1 (p.8-9); BRID_MIG 3.1 (p.9)
* FRS: Data Migration Handbook BRD-13 Data Migration v2.1 (02_BIBS_Handbook_BRD-13_Data_Migration_v2.1.docx), section 20.2 Extract intake, code maps, validation and load, FR-DM-013 Validate staged data against data-quality rules
* Persona: BIBS (validation); Data Steward
* Function: A batch is validated before it can load. Each staged row is mapped and checked against the rules of its object - mandatory fields, formats, lookups, uniqueness, references to loaded parents, cross-field rules (for example components that add up to the gross premium, open balance equal to booked less paid) and plausibility warnings.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Master data may be loaded with at most the error-rate limit of master data percent of rows rejected or waived (default 0.5). (Configurable)
* (R2) Financial objects (open invoices, UPP, GL trial balance) load only with 0 errors, or with each excluded row approved by the data owner with a manual-entry plan. The error rate is (invalid rows not waived + waived rows) / (staged rows - excluded rows); excluded rows are not errors and not in the base. (Configurable)
* (R3) For each component of a legacy invoice - open = booked + adjusted - paid - written off (premium receivable) and open = booked + adjusted - remitted (DTIP and commission). (Fixed)
* Check: Mandatory field blank. Message: "(field) is mandatory"
* Check: Wrong format. Message: "(field) (value) is not a valid (type)"
* Check: Parent not loaded. Message: "(parent) (key) is not loaded"
* Check: Components do not add up. Message: "The premium components add up to (x); the gross premium is (y)"
* Check: Error rate above threshold. Message: "(rate) percent of rows have errors; the limit for this object is (limit) percent"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the batch is Planned with at least one staged extract, when the operator clicks Validate, then a legacy invoice whose components do not add up to its gross premium is Invalid with that message.
* (AC2) Given the batch is Planned with at least one staged extract and a waived row, when the operator clicks Validate, then it shows the waiver reason and the data owner who approved it.
* (AC3) Given the batch is Planned with at least one staged extract and a batch of open invoices with one Invalid row, when the operator clicks Validate, then it cannot be approved for load unless the row is excluded by the data owner; once it is excluded, the error rate shown is 0.00%.

column4: Load a batch through the BIBS services
column6:
As the Data Migration Lead, I need to reconcile all migrated data per data object, so that every data object and item is reconcilable from source to target after the cut-over.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRID_MIG 1.2 (p.7); BRID_MIG 1.3 (p.7-8)
* FRS: Data Migration Handbook BRD-13 Data Migration v2.1 (02_BIBS_Handbook_BRD-13_Data_Migration_v2.1.docx), section 20.2 Extract intake, code maps, validation and load, FR-DM-014 Load a batch through the BIBS services
* Persona: Data Migration Lead (approval); Migration Operator; BIBS (load)
* Function: A validated batch is approved for load (gate G4) and then loaded. Each row is loaded through the same BIBS service that the screens use (for example client registration, account import, the Operations ledger, the unapplied workbench, the journal service), so every BIBS rule, audit entry and accounting entry applies. BIBS never writes directly into business tables.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Rows are loaded in transactions of the rows per load transaction (default 500), in the partitions loaded in parallel (default 4). (Configurable)

column4: Rerun and roll back a batch
column6:
As the Data Migration Lead, I need to remigrate selected or all fall-out records, so that failed or incomplete items are reprocessed and the data is complete.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRID_MIG 1.2 (p.7); BRID_MIG 1.4 (p.8)
* FRS: Data Migration Handbook BRD-13 Data Migration v2.1 (02_BIBS_Handbook_BRD-13_Data_Migration_v2.1.docx), section 20.2 Extract intake, code maps, validation and load, FR-DM-015 Rerun and roll back a batch
* Persona: Data Migration Lead (request); reconciliation approver (approval); Migration Operator
* Function: Rejected rows (the fall-out records of BRID_MIG 1.4) are corrected and loaded again in a rerun batch that belongs to the original batch and is reconciled with it (all rejected rows, or the rows the Data Migration Lead selects). Each row of the rerun shows its result, and the rerun summary gives the rows reprocessed, migrated and failed, with times and error details.

*Business rules*
* (R1) No rollback after the object is accepted (G6); after go-live, corrections are made through the normal business functions. (Fixed)
* (R2) Opening entries are reversed with negative entries of the same event; the original entries stay. (Fixed)
* (R3) A rerun is allowed until the object is accepted (G6) in the cycle; after go-live a financial row that still fails is keyed in BIBS from the manual-entry plan approved by its owner (CLR-DM-13). (Fixed)
* Check: Record changed after load. Message: "(n) records were changed after the load and cannot be rolled back"
* Check: Approver is the requester. Message: "A record cannot be authorized by the user who maintained it"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given Rerun - the batch has rejected rows and corrections are available (new extract, new map version or waiver) and Rollback - the batch is Loaded or Reconciled and not signed off (G6) and a rerun batch, when for a rerun, the Data Migration Lead clicks Rerun Rejects for all rejected rows, or selects rows on the Rows tab first; BIBS creates a child batch with those rows, validates it (dependencies, code maps, data-quality rules) and, after approval, loads it. Each row ends as migrated on the rerun or failed again with its error details (proposed labels, CLR-DM-13), then it loads only the previously rejected rows and its counts are added to the parent batch reconciliation.
* (AC2) Given Rerun - the batch has rejected rows and corrections are available (new extract, new map version or waiver) and Rollback - the batch is Loaded or Reconciled and not signed off (G6), when for a rerun, the Data Migration Lead clicks Rerun Rejects for all rejected rows, or selects rows on the Rows tab first; BIBS creates a child batch with those rows, validates it (dependencies, code maps, data-quality rules) and, after approval, loads it. Each row ends as migrated on the rerun or failed again with its error details (proposed labels, CLR-DM-13), then a rerun of rows selected among the rejected rows reprocesses only those rows; each shows whether it was migrated or failed again, a row that fails again keeps its error details, and the run log gives the counts reprocessed, migrated and failed with the times (BRID_MIG 1.4).
* (AC3) Given Rerun - the batch has rejected rows and corrections are available (new extract, new map version or waiver) and Rollback - the batch is Loaded or Reconciled and not signed off (G6) and a rollback of a client batch without later activity, when for a rerun, the Data Migration Lead clicks Rerun Rejects for all rejected rows, or selects rows on the Rows tab first; BIBS creates a child batch with those rows, validates it (dependencies, code maps, data-quality rules) and, after approval, loads it. Each row ends as migrated on the rerun or failed again with its error details (proposed labels, CLR-DM-13), then it leaves no active migrated client of that batch.
* (AC4) Given Rerun - the batch has rejected rows and corrections are available (new extract, new map version or waiver) and Rollback - the batch is Loaded or Reconciled and not signed off (G6) and a rollback, when for a rerun, the Data Migration Lead clicks Rerun Rejects for all rejected rows, or selects rows on the Rows tab first; BIBS creates a child batch with those rows, validates it (dependencies, code maps, data-quality rules) and, after approval, loads it. Each row ends as migrated on the rerun or failed again with its error details (proposed labels, CLR-DM-13), then it is refused when a payment was applied to a legacy invoice of the batch.

*Out of scope / notes*
* CLR-DM-13 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Remigration of fall-out records (BRID_MIG 1.4). Proposed: Rejected rows are corrected (new extract, new code map version or waiver) and loaded again in a rerun batch linked to the original batch, for all rejected rows or the rows the operator selects; each row shows its result in the rerun (proposed labels 'Migrated on rerun' and 'Failed again'); the run log and the rerun summary give the rows reprocessed, migrated and failed, the times and the error details. column4: Reconcile each data object from source to target
column6:
As the Data Migration Lead, I need to reconcile all migrated data per data object, so that every data object and item is reconcilable from source to target after the cut-over.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRID_MIG 1.2 (p.7)
* FRS: Data Migration Handbook BRD-13 Data Migration v2.1 (02_BIBS_Handbook_BRD-13_Data_Migration_v2.1.docx), section 20.3 Reconciliation, FR-DM-020 Reconcile each data object from source to target
* Persona: Reconciliation approver; BIBS (reconciliation)
* Function: After each load BIBS reconciles the object at four levels, and financial objects at a fifth. L1 counts - control file, received, staged, loaded, skipped, rejected and excluded. L2 amounts - sums per amount column and currency against the control totals and the values in BIBS. L3 hash totals - key column hash and a checksum per row. L4 fields - every mapped field of every loaded row read back from BIBS and compared with the staged value. L5 GL - see FR-DM-021.

*Business rules*
* (R1) L1 - received = control count, and loaded + skipped + rejected + excluded = staged. (Fixed)
* (R2) L2 - amount difference within the amount tolerance (default 0.00) per currency. (Configurable)
* (R3) L4 - a field difference is a break unless the code map explains it (mapped value). (Fixed)
* Check: Sign-off with unexplained break. Message: "Explain and approve every break before signing the reconciliation"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given the batch is Loaded or Loaded with rejects, when BIBS runs the reconciliation after the load, or the approver clicks Reconcile, then for a batch of 1,000 open invoices loaded without rejects, L1 shows 1,000 at every stage and L2 shows 0.00 difference per currency.
* (AC2) Given the batch is Loaded or Loaded with rejects, when BIBS runs the reconciliation after the load, or the approver clicks Reconcile, then a field changed in BIBS after the load appears as an L4 break on the next reconciliation.
* (AC3) Given the batch is Loaded or Loaded with rejects, when BIBS runs the reconciliation after the load, or the approver clicks Reconcile, then the reconciliation cannot be signed while a break has no approved explanation.
* (AC4) Given the batch is Loaded or Loaded with rejects, when BIBS runs the reconciliation after the load, or the approver clicks Reconcile, then the reports Reconciliation Summary and Reconciliation Detail export to Excel and PDF.

column4: Reconcile carried-forward balances to the GL
column6:
As a Cashiering user, I need every legacy unapplied premium payment recorded in BIBS, so that unapplied cash is not lost after the cut-over.

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRID_MIG 1.2 (p.7); BRID_MIG 5.1 (p.9); BRID_MIG 13.1 (p.14)
* FRS: Data Migration Handbook BRD-13 Data Migration v2.1 (02_BIBS_Handbook_BRD-13_Data_Migration_v2.1.docx), section 20.3 Reconciliation, FR-DM-021 Reconcile carried-forward balances to the GL
* Persona: Reconciliation approver (Comptrollership)
* Function: Each open legacy invoice and each legacy UPP item is loaded with an opening entry against the Migration Clearing account. The GL trial balance of the legacy systems is loaded as an opening journal in which the lines of the legacy control accounts are replaced by Migration Clearing. When the detail and the trial balance agree, Migration Clearing is 0.00 per branch and currency.

*Business rules*
* (R1) Migration Clearing must be 0.00 per branch and currency before go-live. (Fixed)
* (R2) The legacy control accounts and the Migration Clearing account are set up by Comptrollership; the GL account code map says which legacy accounts go to Migration Clearing. (Configurable)
* (R3) A difference on Migration Clearing has the sign of the trial balance - for an invoice missing from the load, a debit equal to its net receivable position (open PR + PR2307 + commission receivable - open DTIP - unrealised commission - deferred VAT) when positive, a credit when negative; for a missing UPP item, a credit equal to its balance. (Fixed)
* (R4) The report Migration Clearing and Legacy Control Accounts also compares, per branch, currency and legacy control account, the trial balance line with the opening detail posted to that account, so a missing invoice whose net is zero is still found. (Fixed)
* (R5) The same checks run again after each FY2027 true-up (FR-DM-024). (Fixed)
* Check: Clearing not zero at sign-off. Message: "Migration Clearing is (amount) in (branch) (currency); it must be zero"
* Check: Control account line differs from the detail. Message: "(account) differs from the opening detail by (amount) in (branch) (currency)"

*Acceptance criteria*
* (AC1) Given Open invoices, UPP and the GL trial balance are loaded for the environment, when the approver runs the report Migration Clearing and Legacy Control Accounts, then after the loads of open invoices, UPP and the trial balance of a branch, Migration Clearing is 0.00 in PHP and USD.
* (AC2) Given Open invoices, UPP and the GL trial balance are loaded for the environment, when the approver runs the report Migration Clearing and Legacy Control Accounts, then the ACSL reconciliation of the legacy Premium Receivable account against the legacy invoices shows no difference.
* (AC3) Given Open invoices, UPP and the GL trial balance are loaded for the environment, when the approver runs the report Migration Clearing and Legacy Control Accounts, then the Premium Receivable, DTIP, Commission Receivable and unapplied-payment balances of the opening equal the legacy trial balance and the legacy sub-ledgers per branch and currency with a difference of 0.00 (BRID_MIG 13.1; tolerance CLR-DM-04).
* (AC4) Given Open invoices, UPP and the GL trial balance are loaded for the environment, when the approver runs the report Migration Clearing and Legacy Control Accounts, then an invoice paid in full and not remitted, with 5,000.00 open DTIP and 800.00 commission receivable, missing from the load leaves a credit of 4,200.00 on Migration Clearing; an unpaid invoice with 3,000.00 premium receivable and 3,000.00 DTIP missing from the load leaves Migration Clearing at 0.00 and shows a 3,000.00 difference on Premium Receivable - Legacy and on DTIP - Legacy.

*Out of scope / notes*
* CLR-DM-04 - open, for BDOI confirmation: Reconciliation tolerance and 'no material variances'. Proposed: BRID_MIG 13.1 accepts the accounting data 'with no material variances'. The set keeps an amount tolerance of 0.00 per currency for every object (PR-DM-28) and no materiality threshold: every difference is a break that is fixed by a rerun or explained and approved by the reconciliation approver before gate G5 Decision requested: The Head of Comptrollership confirms the 0.00 tolerance, or names the threshold and the objects it applies to

column4: Load the provisional GL opening at the year-end boundary
column6:
As the Program Manager, I need the cut-over aligned to the renewal expiry month (RMEL), so that in-force policies run off and renew into BIBS in a controlled manner.

*Background*

* Persona: Head, Comptrollership; Migration Operator
* Function: For a go-live on 3 January 2028 at the year-end boundary (DMQ39, option A, recommended and awaiting Comptrollership confirmation), the BIBS GL opens from the preliminary December 2027 trial balance of legacy, taken after the December soft close and the last legacy EOD. Only the balance-sheet accounts are opened. The FY2027 P&L accounts are not opened; their net result per branch and currency goes to retained earnings, so the FY2028 P&L in BIBS starts at zero.

*Business rules*
* (R1) The opening journals are system journals of type Opening, source Migration, value date the opening value date (default 1 January 2028, the first day of the opening period). (Configurable)
* (R2) No FY2027 P&L balance is opened in BIBS; a line whose mapped account is a P&L account posts to retained earnings, with the mapped account kept in the line description. (Fixed)
* (R3) The opening stays marked Provisional until the closure of the true-ups (FR-DM-024). (Fixed)

* Check: Retained earnings account missing. Message: "The retained earnings account of the company is not set"

* (AC2) Given the GL account code map is approved and the company's retained earnings account is set and Comptrollership has signed the preliminary December trial balance as the provisional opening and a legacy trial balance with a FY2027 net income of 1,250,000.00 in a branch, when the operator validates and loads G01 (trial balance version Provisional), then it gives a credit of 1,250,000.00 to retained earnings in that branch.

* (AC4) Given the GL account code map is approved and the company's retained earnings account is set and Comptrollership has signed the preliminary December trial balance as the provisional opening, when the operator validates and loads G01 (trial balance version Provisional), then the opening journals show the flag Provisional until the true-ups are closed.

column4: Post the FY2027 true-ups as opening-balance adjustment journals
column6:

*Background*
* BRD references and pages: BRID_MIG 1.2 (p.7); BRID_MIG 5.1 (p.9); BRID_MIG 12.1 (p.13); BRID_MIG 13.1 (p.14)
* FRS: Data Migration Handbook BRD-13 Data Migration v2.1 (02_BIBS_Handbook_BRD-13_Data_Migration_v2.1.docx), section 20.3 Reconciliation, FR-DM-023 Post the FY2027 true-ups as opening-balance adjustment journals
* Persona: Comptrollership GL lead (prepares); Head, Comptrollership (approves); Migration Operator
* Function: After the freeze the legacy GL stays open only for the FY2027 closing and audit adjustments, restricted to named Comptrollership users, with no new business. Each adjustment reaches BIBS in a true-up - the first after the legacy year-end close (about mid to late January 2028), the final one after the audited financial statements (about March-April 2028), and interim ones only when Comptrollership posts material adjustments in between.

*Business rules*
* (R1) A true-up posts as a system journal of type Opening, source Migration, reference MIG-TU-<n>-<branch>-<currency>, value date the opening value date (1 January 2028). (Fixed)
* (R2) FY2027 P&L lines post to retained earnings. Lines on legacy control accounts post to Migration Clearing and are matched by the open-item detail, which changes the open balance of each legacy invoice or UPP item (movement Legacy adjusted or Legacy written off) against Migration Clearing. (Fixed)
* (R3) Only journals dated in FY2027, posted in legacy after the freeze and entered in the FY2027 adjustment register are accepted. (Fixed)
* (R4) The preparer and the approver are different users; the approver holds the permission Data migration trueup approve. (Fixed)
* (R5) Posting happens once per reference; the same true-up posted twice creates no second journal. (Fixed)

* Check: Journal not in the register. Message: "Journal (no) is not in the FY2027 adjustment register"
* Check: Journal out of balance. Message: "Journal (no) is out of balance by (amount) in (branch) (currency)"
* Check: Control-account line without detail. Message: "(account) adjustment of (amount) has no matching open-item detail"
* Check: Detail beyond the item balance. Message: "Adjustment of (component) on (item) makes the open balance (amount)"
* Check: Approver is the preparer. Message: "A record cannot be authorized by the user who maintained it"

* (AC2) Given the provisional opening is loaded (FR-DM-022) and BDOI IT has sent, each with its control file, the legacy trial balance after the adjustments (G01, version TU1, TU2 or Final), the adjustment journal lines since the previous true-up (G03), the open-item detail of the lines on legacy control accounts (G03D) and the legacy journal listing since the freeze, when the operator runs the intake checks and the validation of the true-up batch, then an audit write-off of 3,000.00 of premium receivable on legacy invoice I00300002, sent with its detail line, reduces the open basic premium of the invoice and Premium Receivable - Legacy by 3,000.00 and leaves Migration Clearing at 0.00.
* (AC3) Given the provisional opening is loaded (FR-DM-022) and BDOI IT has sent, each with its control file, the legacy trial balance after the adjustments (G01, version TU1, TU2 or Final), the adjustment journal lines since the previous true-up (G03), the open-item detail of the lines on legacy control accounts (G03D) and the legacy journal listing since the freeze, when the operator runs the intake checks and the validation of the true-up batch, then a journal dated 5 January 2028, or a journal not in the register, stops the validation with its message.
